steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Muslims believe in qadr (predestination) — that Allah has foreknowledge and control over all things. However, most Muslims also believe humans have free will to choose their actions. The relationship between God's decree and human freedom is one of the most debated topics in Islamic theology.

steps.title: Exam Tip
steps.body: The key tension: if Allah has already decreed everything, how can humans be responsible for their actions? Most Muslims resolve this by saying Allah's foreknowledge is not the same as forcing — he knows what you will freely choose. You are still responsible.

steps.title: RS Exam Tips — Predestination and Free Will
steps.body: 1. For Predestination and Free Will questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of Predestination and Free Will to its real-world impact on believers and society

steps.title: UK Context
steps.body: When a British Muslim says ‘insha’Allah’ (‘if Allah wills’) when discussing future plans, they are acknowledging al-qadr — that nothing happens except by Allah’s permission. This does not mean they believe their efforts are pointless; rather, it expresses trust in Allah’s wisdom while still taking responsibility for their actions.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain two Muslim beliefs about predestination and free will. | "If God knows everything, humans do not have free will." Evaluate this statement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always refer to specific sources of authority (scripture, sacred texts, religious leaders) Explain contrasting beliefs — different views within and between traditions Use key terminology precisely (e.g. tawhid, atonement, sanctity of life) For 12-mark evaluation questions, consider both sides before reaching a justified conclusion Link beliefs to their impact on individuals, communities and society Acknowledge diversity — no religious tradition has a single, uniform view
